chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from one of his companions, who said:
It is recommended that there be in his shroud a garment in which he used to pray, clean, for that is recommended: that he be shrouded in what he used to pray in.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for selecting clothing for a Muslim's shroud according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to highlight the virtue of linking the deceased’s final state with their daily devotion, specifically recommending a clean garment used for prayer as part of the kafan. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on continuity in worship and the sanctity of items associated with salah, reinforcing the idea that the body should be prepared in a manner that mirrors its spiritual purpose. The recommendation underscores the belief that such garments carry a residual blessing (barakah) from their frequent use in proximity to God.
